name: NE-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+27 partisan lean in a heavily Republican western Nebraska district
Incumbent Adrian Smith running again with a large financial edge ($1.8M raised vs $55K)
No outside spending against Smith and no general-election polling
Prediction markets price Smith at roughly 97% to win
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Smith: a R+27 district, incumbency, and a fundraising advantage of more than 30-to-1, with no outside opposition spending. Markets and the absence of any serious Democratic infrastructure both point to a Safe R outcome.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Smith or an unusually strong Democratic environment in Nebraska could narrow the margin, though not plausibly enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Western Nebraska's third district is one of the most Republican seats in the country, with a partisan lean of R+27. Adrian Smith has held the seat since 2007 and is running again with the advantages of incumbency and a dominant financial position: he has raised about $1.8 million and holds over $1 million on hand, while Democrat Becky Stille has raised roughly $55,000 with minimal cash remaining. No outside groups are spending against Smith.

There is no general-election polling in the race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive. Prediction markets give Smith about a 97% chance of winning. The forecast expects Smith to win by roughly 21 points, consistent with the district's fundamentals, and classifies the race as Safe R.
